```{r config-id}
#| include: false

# ===========================================================================
#  PARAMETERS  --  single source of truth for this document.
#  Every tunable knob lives in THIS block.  Nothing tunable is defined in the
#  setup or data-prep chunks (or anywhere else); they only CONSUME these
#  values.  The DERIVED section below builds everything from them; do not edit
#  it.  This chunk runs first and is `include: false`, so CONFIG_ID is
#  available to the inline prose; the visible echoes of these
#  settings are printed by the setup chunk.
# ===========================================================================

## -- Scenario & sample size --------------------------------------------------
scenario <- "actg175_binary_m1c_harm_adjusted_resample"
sim_n    <- 500

## -- Master seed -------------------------------------------------------------
seed_base <- 8316951L         # master RNG seed (applied via set.seed in setup)
analysis_seed <- seed_base    # RNG seed for the single-trial LOO / Kfold deep-dive
                              # (forestsearch_Kfold seedit=); defaults to the master seed
run_single_trial <- TRUE      # FALSE skips the single-trial alt/null deep-dives
                              # (sim + bootstrap + LOO + Pareto) for fast dev
                              # iteration; keep TRUE -- this document IS the
                              # single-trial sanity check (alt + null only).

## -- Forestsearch base config ------------------------------------------------
fs_tag            <- "fs3c"    # _fsparams/<fs_tag>_params.R supplies the base bundle
fs_sg_focus       <- "effMaxSG"
fs_selection_rule <- "both"   # "neighborhood" | "pareto" | "both"; eff focus
                              # auto-reverts to "neighborhood" (see DERIVED)

## -- Forestsearch effect / consistency thresholds (override fs3) -------------
# The search is most sensitive to these; they override whatever fs3 sets.
fs_effect_threshold       <- 1.25   # SCREENING:   candidate subgroup OR must exceed
fs_consistency_threshold  <- 1.0   # CONSISTENCY: each bootstrap split OR must exceed
fs_pconsistency_threshold <- 0.90   # CONS. RATE:  fraction of splits that must hold

## -- Covariate adjustment (NEW knob; set HERE, not in fs3b_params.R) ----------
# Baseline covariates the forestsearch outcome model adjusts for during BOTH
# candidate search and consistency.  Binary/OR path: the effect-estimator fits
# a logistic model  y ~ treat + <fs_adjust_covariates>  and reports the
# treatment log-OR.  Set NULL for the unadjusted model.
fs_adjust_covariates <- c("cd40", "wtkg")

## -- Consistency calculation method (split vs. resampling) -------------------
# "split"    -- literal repeated 50/50 split-and-refit consistency (original).
# "resample" -- multiplier (influence-function / dfbeta) approximation of the
#               SAME rate via consistency_resample().  For this binary/OR
#               document the resampling path now ENGAGES directly: each
#               candidate subgroup is fit once by the logistic effect-estimator,
#               and the consistency rate is the closed form
#               2*Phi((beta - log c2) / sigma_D) - 1, where beta is the
#               treatment log-OR and sigma_D its robust (sandwich) SE -- no
#               split-and-refit loop.  Configurations the approximation cannot
#               represent as a single coefficient (IRD, propensity-adjusted, or
#               non-convergent fits) fall back to literal splitting automatically.

fs_consistency_method <- "resample"

## -- Single-trial method check (split vs. resample) --------------------------
# When TRUE, the single-trial section re-runs the flagship arm under both
# consistency_method settings and reports the selected subgroup, size, timing,
# and per-candidate consistency rates side by side.  Set FALSE to skip the
# extra forestsearch runs.
fs_run_method_compare <- TRUE

## -- De-biased selection gate (Tier-2 test) ----------------------------------
# Fast multiplier-bootstrap de-biased estimate + selection gate, validated
# against the full (Tier-1) bootstrap on this single trial.  Requires
# fdr_family_multiplier.R, fdr_calibration.R, and fdr_debias_gate.R on the path
# (set options(fdr_src_dir = "<dir>") if they are not beside this .qmd).
run_debias_gate <- TRUE


## -- Methods set & flagship arm ----------------------------------------------
# Any subset of <engine>-<focus>, engine in {fs, dina, grf}, focus in
# {eff, effMaxSG, effMinSG}, plus the special "grf-tree".
METHODS <- c(
  "fs-eff",   "fs-effMaxSG", "fs-effMinSG",
  "dina-eff", "dina-effMaxSG", "dina-effMinSG",
  "grf-eff",  "grf-effMaxSG", "grf-effMinSG",
  "grf-tree"
)
FLAGSHIP_ARM <- "fs-effMaxSG"   # arm spotlighted in the per-arm distribution
                                # displays (subgroup-cut + OR distribution, H1/H0)
                                # and recorded in the bundle meta.  The comparison
                                # tables (detection/classification/estimation)
                                # remain all-methods.  Must be a full <engine>-<focus>
                                # arm in METHODS.

## -- Depth / fairness (every engine searches the same 2-factor space) --------
grf_depth           <- 2L
dina_max_depth      <- 2L
dina_grid_probs     <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1)
effect_neighborhood <- 0.10   # frontier / neighborhood selection band

## -- GRF SELECTION floors for the forestsearch-routed grf-* arms -------------
# dmin.grf is a SELECTION floor (not screening); 0.0 is permissive, raise to
# calibrate.  Binary-OR DR-score scale.
grf_screen_dmin   <- 0.0      # fs-* arms (screening floor)
grf_tree_dmin     <- 0.10     # grf-tree
grf_frontier_dmin <- 0.10     # grf-eff / grf-effMaxSG / grf-effMinSG (frontier)

## -- Standalone GRF parameters (legacy standalone GRF; recorded in meta) -----
grf_dmin         <- 0.10
grf_maxdepth     <- 2L
grf_sg_criterion <- "mDiff"

## -- Calibration -------------------------------------------------------------
cal_target_or <- 2.0          # target marginal OR in the harm subgroup Q

## -- Reporting / display -----------------------------------------------------
sg_notation     <- "harm"
display_digits  <- 3
frontier_params <- list(
  n_splits = 1000L, seed = 1L, xlim = c(1.0, 5.0),
  digits_effect = 2L, digits_pcons = 2L, digits_ci = 2L
)

## -- Subgroup- / effect-distribution plot thresholds -------------------------
sgdist_min_pct_alt  <- 0
sgdist_min_pct_null <- 0
sgdist_top_k        <- 20L
ordist_ylim         <- c(0, 4)

## -- Diagnostic capture ------------------------------------------------------
diag_keep         <- c("fs_full", "candidate_table")
diag_keep_first_n <- 5L

## -- Parallel ----------------------------------------------------------------
worker_fraction <- 0.95       # fraction of PHYSICAL cores for the MC outer loop

# ===========================================================================
#  DERIVED  --  built from the PARAMETERS above.  Do not edit.
# ===========================================================================

n_workers <- max(1L, floor(worker_fraction * parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)))

## fs_params: source the canonical fs3 bundle, then apply the visible overrides.
## Both the preferred names (effect.threshold/consistency.threshold) and the
## hr.* aliases are set so any code reading either stays in sync.
source(sprintf("_fsparams/%s_params.R", fs_tag))
fs_params <- get(sprintf("get_%s_params", fs_tag))(sg_focus = fs_sg_focus)
fs_params$effect.threshold       <- fs_effect_threshold
fs_params$hr.threshold           <- fs_effect_threshold
fs_params$consistency.threshold  <- fs_consistency_threshold
fs_params$hr.consistency         <- fs_consistency_threshold
fs_params$pconsistency.threshold <- fs_pconsistency_threshold
# selection_rule "pareto"/"both" require a directional focus; the eff base
# focus supports "neighborhood" only (forestsearch errors otherwise).  Mirrors
# the .rule_for() guard used per-arm below.  Governs the flagship deep-dive.
fs_params$selection_rule <-
  if (fs_sg_focus %in% c("effMaxSG", "effMinSG")) fs_selection_rule else "neighborhood"

## Covariate adjustment: inject the qmd-level knob into the SHARED fs_params
## base so it reaches forestsearch() for every fs-* arm (the consistency engine
## honours it via the logistic effect-estimator).  grf-* and dina-* arms do not
## use that estimator for selection, so the term is inert for their selection --
## the comparison contrasts an ADJUSTED forestsearch against unadjusted
## GRF/DINA selection, which is intentional.  NULL leaves the model unadjusted.
fs_params$adjust_covariates <- fs_adjust_covariates

## Consistency method: inject the qmd-level knob into the SHARED fs_params base
## so it reaches forestsearch() (consistency_method=) for every fs-* arm.  On
## this binary/OR document forestsearch threads a GLM resample spec to the
## consistency engine, so "resample" engages the logistic dfbeta approximation
## directly; unsupported measures (IRD, PS-adjusted, non-convergent) fall back
## to literal splitting automatically.
fs_params$consistency_method <- fs_consistency_method

## Methods spec: every arm runs THROUGH forestsearch(), tagged "<engine>-<focus>".
## fs_params is the SHARED base; make_methods supplies per-arm overrides.  The
## grf-* arms are forestsearch's GRF policy-tree / frontier selector (NOT the
## legacy standalone grf.subg.harm.glm).
make_methods <- function(labels) {
  spec <- list()
  .rule_for <- function(focus) {
    if (focus %in% c("effMaxSG", "effMinSG")) fs_selection_rule else "neighborhood"
  }
  for (lbl in labels) {
    parts  <- strsplit(lbl, "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
    engine <- parts[1L]; focus <- paste(parts[-1L], collapse = "-")
    if (engine == "fs") {
      spec[[lbl]] <- list(subgroup_method = "consistency", sg_focus = focus,
                          selection_rule = .rule_for(focus),
                          dmin.grf = grf_screen_dmin)
    } else if (engine == "dina") {
      spec[[lbl]] <- list(subgroup_method = "dina", sg_focus = focus,
                          selection_rule = .rule_for(focus),
                          effect_neighborhood = effect_neighborhood,
                          dina_args = list(max_depth = dina_max_depth,
                                           grid_probs = dina_grid_probs))
    } else if (engine == "grf") {
      if (identical(focus, "tree")) {
        spec[[lbl]] <- list(subgroup_method = "grf", grf_selection = "tree",
                            grf_depth = grf_depth, dmin.grf = grf_tree_dmin,
                            use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE)
      } else {
        spec[[lbl]] <- list(subgroup_method = "grf", grf_selection = "frontier",
                            sg_focus = focus, grf_depth = grf_depth,
                            selection_rule = .rule_for(focus),
                            dmin.grf = grf_frontier_dmin,
                            effect_neighborhood = effect_neighborhood,
                            use_grf = FALSE, use_lasso = FALSE)
      }
    } else stop(sprintf("Unknown engine in label '%s'.", lbl), call. = FALSE)
  }
  spec
}
METHODS_SPEC <- make_methods(METHODS)

## Flagship must be one of METHODS.  Hard-error on an invalid value rather than
## silently falling back to METHODS[1L] -- a bad FLAGSHIP_ARM otherwise masks itself.
if (!FLAGSHIP_ARM %in% METHODS) {
  stop(sprintf(
    "FLAGSHIP_ARM = '%s' is not one of METHODS (%s).\n  Use a full '<engine>-<focus>' arm name, e.g. 'fs-effMaxSG'.",
    FLAGSHIP_ARM, paste(METHODS, collapse = ", ")),
    call. = FALSE)
}

## Fairness self-check: every engine must search the SAME depth.
.fs_maxk <- if (!is.null(fs_params$maxk)) fs_params$maxk else 2L
if (.fs_maxk != dina_max_depth || grf_depth != dina_max_depth) {
  warning(sprintf(
    paste0("Depth fairness mismatch: fs maxk = %s, grf_depth = %d, ",
           "dina max_depth = %d.  Engines are searching different spaces; ",
           "set them equal for a fair comparison."),
    .fs_maxk, grf_depth, dina_max_depth), call. = FALSE)
}

## Config id (single-trial document; no bundle is written).
CONFIG_ID <- sprintf("%s_%s_n%d_single-simtrial", scenario, fs_tag, sim_n)
```

This article runs the **single-trial sanity check** for configuration
**`` `r CONFIG_ID` ``** (study = ACTG175, outcome = binary,
DGM = m1 [calibrated GLM, target OR(Q) = 2.0], objective = harm,
FS bundle = `r fs_tag`).  It is a trimmed version of the full
multi-method study: it keeps data preparation, DGM calibration, and the
single-trial deep-dives under the alternative (H1) and the null (H0) --
each running every method through `forestsearch()` once on one simulated
trial, with the bootstrap, LOO cross-validation, and Pareto worked
examples -- and omits the Monte-Carlo simulation study, the operating-
characteristics tables, and all bundle saving.

Data preparation, DGM calibration, and both single-trial deep-dives run
unconditionally; nothing is written to disk.

**Covariate-adjusted variant.** This configuration adjusts the
forestsearch outcome model for
`` `r if (is.null(fs_adjust_covariates)) "none" else paste(fs_adjust_covariates, collapse = ", ")` ``
(logistic `y ~ treat + covariates`, treatment log-OR reported) during
search and consistency, and the bootstrap / Kfold / estimate-table
re-estimation inherit the same adjustment.

**Consistency method.** This variant sets `consistency_method = "resample"`,
the multiplier-bootstrap approximation of the splitting-consistency rate.
For binary/OR outcomes the approximation now engages directly: each candidate
subgroup is fit once by the logistic effect-estimator, and the consistency
rate is obtained in closed form from the treatment log-OR $\hat\beta$ and its
robust (sandwich) standard error $\sigma_D$,
$2\Phi\!\big((\hat\beta - \log c_2)/\sigma_D\big) - 1$, rather than by
repeated 50/50 split-and-refit.  Configurations the approximation cannot
represent as a single coefficient (IRD, propensity-adjusted effects, or
non-convergent fits) fall back to literal splitting automatically, so a
consistency rate is always produced.  @sec-method-check re-runs the
single trial under both settings to confirm they select the same subgroup
with consistency rates agreeing to within the documented approximation error.

```{r setup}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Libraries, derived locals, echoes (all parameters are in the config-id block)"

library(forestsearch)
library(speff2trial)
library(data.table)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
library(future)
library(doFuture)
library(foreach)

# ALL tunable parameters live in the `config-id` block at the top of the
# document (single source of truth).  This chunk only loads libraries, sets the
# seed, echoes the active settings, and builds a few locals consumed by later
# chunks.

set.seed(seed_base)

# This trimmed document runs ONLY the single-trial deep-dives (no Monte-Carlo
# study and no bundle).  sim_mode / nsims_* are defined here purely so the
# Timing Summary subtitle can report them; they drive no computation.
sim_mode   <- "single-trial"
nsims_alt  <- 0L
nsims_null <- 0L

# -- Echo active settings ----------------------------------------------------
cat(sprintf("mode = single-trial (alt + null) | sim_n = %d\n", sim_n))
cat(sprintf(
  "FS thresholds -> screening OR >= %.2f | consistency OR >= %.2f | rate >= %.0f%%\n",
  fs_effect_threshold, fs_consistency_threshold, 100 * fs_pconsistency_threshold))

# DINA harm floor (m_diff): the dina-* arms set no threshold of their own, so
# they inherit fs_effect_threshold via fs_params.  Inside forestsearch the DINA
# selector maps that screening threshold to the link scale -- log() for ratio
# measures (OR/HR/IRR), identity for difference measures (MD/RD/IRD).  The
# package's own scale test is used so this echo matches what dina_subgroup()
# actually clears.  All three dina-* arms share this floor; they differ only in
# sg_focus / selection_rule / effect_neighborhood.
.dina_identity <- forestsearch:::is_identity_scale(fs_params$effect_measure)
dina_m_diff    <- if (.dina_identity) fs_effect_threshold else log(fs_effect_threshold)
cat(sprintf(
  "DINA harm floor -> m_diff = %.4f  (link scale; %s)\n",
  dina_m_diff,
  if (.dina_identity)
    sprintf("identity = %.4g for %s", fs_effect_threshold, fs_params$effect_measure)
  else
    sprintf("log(%.2f) for %s", fs_effect_threshold, fs_params$effect_measure)))

# -- Derived locals consumed by later chunks ---------------------------------
grf_params <- list(
  dmin.grf     = grf_dmin,
  maxdepth     = grf_maxdepth,
  sg.criterion = grf_sg_criterion
)

# Re-exposed for the single-trial sanity-check chunks.
c1       <- fs_params$hr.threshold
max_look <- fs_params$max_subgroups_search

# Display helper: tidy a cut-string for DISPLAY only (rounds full-precision
# numeric thresholds to `digits` significant figures; collapses whitespace,
# leaves integer cuts untouched).  Used by the subgroup-distribution renders.
tidy_sg_def <- function(s, digits = 4L) {
  if (length(s) != 1L || is.na(s) || !nzchar(s)) return(s)
  s <- gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", s)
  m <- gregexpr("-?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+", s)[[1L]]
  if (m[1L] == -1L) return(s)
  L <- attr(m, "match.length")
  for (i in rev(seq_along(m))) {
    num <- as.numeric(substr(s, m[i], m[i] + L[i] - 1L))
    rep <- sub("\\.$", "", formatC(signif(num, digits), format = "fg", flag = "#"))
    s <- paste0(substr(s, 1L, m[i] - 1L), rep, substr(s, m[i] + L[i], nchar(s)))
  }
  s
}

# Document-level timing accumulator; each major chunk populates its slot, and
# the bottom-of-document Timing Summary renders the collated values ("—" if unset).
timings <- list()
```

```{r pareto-prep}
#| include: false

library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)

# Loaded for the validation section; the figure itself is self-contained.
have_fs <- requireNamespace("forestsearch", quietly = TRUE)

EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD <- 0.10   # the package default

# Mirror of forestsearch internal .pareto_dominated_xy(): both axes maximized.
dominated_xy <- function(x, y) {
  n <- length(x)
  dom <- logical(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (is.na(x[i]) || is.na(y[i])) { dom[i] <- TRUE; next }
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (i == j) next
      if (is.na(x[j]) || is.na(y[j])) next
      if (x[j] >= x[i] && y[j] >= y[i] && (x[j] > x[i] || y[j] > y[i])) {
        dom[i] <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
  }
  dom
}
```

# Purpose

`forestsearch()` (and, since v0.2.0, `dina_subgroup()`) selects among the
qualifying candidate subgroups using `sg_focus`. For the effect-anchored
foci `"effMaxSG"`/`"effMinSG"` (canonical `"hrMaxSG"`/`"hrMinSG"`), the
selection is *not* "take the candidate with the largest effect." Instead
the candidates are first partitioned into a **candidate inclusion band**,
and then ranked within that band by sample size. The `selection_rule`
argument controls how the band is drawn:

* `"neighborhood"` --- a one-dimensional effect band (default).
* `"pareto"` --- the two-dimensional Pareto-non-dominated set in
  (effect, $N$) space.
* `"both"` --- the intersection of the two (strictest).

This note explains how the **Pareto frontier** operates: what
"dominated" means, how the frontier becomes the `in_pareto` indicator,
how it combines with the neighborhood band, and how the resulting
`in_band` flag feeds the final selection sort. The single computation
shared by every path is `.compute_inclusion_band()`, called by both
`sort_subgroups()` (final, post-consistency selection) and
`sort_subgroups_preview()` (pre-consistency triage).

# A worked candidate set

Five candidates that have already passed the consistency stage and the
effect threshold. Effect on the natural (HR) scale, size $N$:

```{r candidates}
cands <- data.table(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "F"),
  hr = c(2.50, 2.40, 2.30, 2.35, 2.00),
  N  = c(70L,  100L, 150L, 90L,  200L)
)

hr_max  <- max(cands$hr)
hr_floor <- (1 - EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD) * hr_max

cands[, in_nbhd     := hr >= hr_floor]
cands[, dominated   := dominated_xy(hr, N)]
cands[, on_frontier := !dominated]
cands[, in_both     := in_nbhd & on_frontier]
cands[, status      := fifelse(!in_nbhd, "neither (below floor)",
                        fifelse(in_both,  "both rules",
                                          "neighborhood only"))]

# effMaxSG within the "both" band: largest N among in-band-both candidates.
sel_id <- cands[in_both == TRUE][order(-N)][1L, id]
cands[, selected := id == sel_id]

cands[, .(id, hr, N, in_nbhd, on_frontier, in_both, selected)]
```

With `hr_max = 2.5`, the floor is `r round(hr_floor, 3)`. So:

* `A`, `B`, `C` are in the effect band **and** on the frontier --- in-band
  under every rule.
* `E` (HR 2.35, $N$ 90) is in the effect band but **dominated by `B`**
  (HR 2.40 $\ge$ 2.35 and $N$ 100 $\ge$ 90), so `"pareto"`/`"both"`
  exclude it while `"neighborhood"` keeps it.
* `F` (HR 2.00, $N$ 200) is on the frontier (largest $N$) but **below the
  floor**, so `"neighborhood"`/`"both"` exclude it while `"pareto"`
  keeps it --- this is the over-extension guard that the effect band
  provides and the bare frontier does not.

# The figure

```{r}
#| label: fig-frontier
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-cap: "Candidate subgroups in the (effect, N) plane. The shaded region is the effect neighborhood band (HR at least the dashed floor); the dashed line traces the Pareto frontier. Colour encodes which selection_rule keeps each candidate. C is selected by effMaxSG (largest N in the band)."

pal <- c("both rules"           = "#1D9E75",
         "neighborhood only"    = "#EF9F27",
         "neither (below floor)" = "#888780")

frontier <- cands[on_frontier == TRUE][order(hr)]

# per-point label offsets so the letters sit clear of points/lines
labs <- data.table(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "E", "F"),
  lx = c(2.50, 2.435, 2.30, 2.35, 2.00),
  ly = c(63,   108,   166,  79,   210))

ggplot(cands, aes(hr, N)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = hr_floor, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#378ADD", alpha = 0.10) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = hr_floor, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#185FA5", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = frontier, aes(hr, N), linetype = "dashed",
            colour = "#888780", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = cands[selected == TRUE], aes(hr, N),
             shape = 21, size = 9, stroke = 1.3,
             colour = "#0F6E56", fill = NA) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = status), size = 3.6) +
  geom_text(data = labs, aes(lx, ly, label = id),
            size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = hr_floor + 0.015, y = 219,
           label = sprintf("HR >= %.2f  (within %.0f%% of max)",
                           hr_floor, 100 * EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.1, colour = "#185FA5") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal, name = "in_band under") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1.9, 2.62)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(45, 222)) +
  labs(x = "effect (HR)", y = "subgroup size N") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

Reading the figure: `"neighborhood"` keeps the whole shaded strip
$\{A, B, C, E\}$; `"both"` additionally drops `E` because it sits
*inside* the frontier (another point beats it on both axes); `"pareto"`
alone would keep `F` (top-left, on the frontier) despite its weak
effect. The selection then maximizes $N$ within the kept set.


# Data Preparation {#sec-data}

```{r data-prep}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "ACTG175 data prep (click to expand)"

# ACTG175: arm 1 = ZDV+ddI (experimental), arm 3 = ddI (control)
actg_df <- subset(speff2trial::ACTG175, arms %in% c(1L, 3L))
actg_df$id <- seq_len(nrow(actg_df))

# Treatment: ZDV+ddI = 1, ddI = 0 (NO switching)
actg_df$treat <- ifelse(actg_df$arms == 1L, 1L, 0L)

# Binary outcome: adverse (failure to improve)
actg_df$y_binary <- as.integer(actg_df$cd420 <= actg_df$cd40)
actg_df <- actg_df[!is.na(actg_df$cd420), ]

# -- DGM factor variables -----------------------------------------------------
# Note that binary and continuous analyses are similar in identified subgroups
# (from observed-data FS result — see companion analysis document)

 actg_df$z1  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$cd40 > 390, 1L, 0L))
 actg_df$z2  <- as.factor(ifelse(actg_df$wtkg > 80, 1L, 0L))

# z7-z12: truly binary indicators (no continuous counterpart)
actg_df$z7  <- as.factor(actg_df$hemo)
actg_df$z8  <- as.factor(actg_df$homo)
actg_df$z9  <- as.factor(actg_df$drugs)
actg_df$z10 <- as.factor(actg_df$race)
actg_df$z11 <- as.factor(actg_df$gender)
actg_df$z12 <- as.factor(actg_df$symptom)

actg_df$ar_naive   <- as.integer(ifelse(actg_df$str2 == 0, 1L, 0L))
actg_df$prior_6mo  <- as.integer(ifelse(actg_df$preanti <= 6 * 30.4375, 1L, 0L))

actg_df$flag_harm_ref <- as.integer(actg_df$z1 == 1 & actg_df$z2 == 1)

# -- Analysis covariates (what the analyst sees) -------------------------------
cont_vars <- c("age", "preanti", "wtkg", "karnof", "cd40", "cd80")
bin_vars  <- c("hemo", "homo", "drugs", "race", "gender", "symptom","ar_naive","prior_6mo")
# Binary confounders kept NUMERIC 0/1: the forestsearch-routed dina-* arms
# require numeric covariates, and grf-* cut-strings (e.g. "symptom <= 0") must
# be numeric to evaluate.  z7-z12 (created above) stay factors for the DGM.
for (v in bin_vars) actg_df[[v]] <- as.integer(actg_df[[v]])
confounders <- c(cont_vars, bin_vars)


# -- DGM variable sets ---------------------------------------------------------
dgm_factor_vars   <- c("z1", "z2", paste0("z", 7:12))
dgm_cont_vars     <- cont_vars
dgm_subgroup_vars <- c("z1", "z2")
dgm_subgroup_cuts <- list(z1 = 1L, z2 = 1L)

# -- Summary -------------------------------------------------------------------
Q_n   <- sum(actg_df$flag_harm_ref)
Q_N   <- nrow(actg_df)
Q_pct <- 100 * Q_n / Q_N

cat(sprintf("N = %d, Q prevalence = %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n", Q_N, Q_n, Q_N, Q_pct))
cat(sprintf("Adverse rate: overall=%.1f%%, ZDV+ddI=%.1f%%, ddI=%.1f%%\n",
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary),
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat == 1]),
    100 * mean(actg_df$y_binary[actg_df$treat == 0])))
```

# DGM Calibration {#sec-calibration}

Target: OR(Q) = `r cal_target_or` on the adverse scale.  The DGM
includes factor variables (for subgroup definition) and raw continuous
covariates (for a richer prognostic baseline), consistent with the
survival `generate_aft_dgm_flex()` design.

```{r calibrate}
dgm_calibrated <- calibrate_glm_interaction(
  data            = actg_df,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  continuous_vars = dgm_cont_vars,
  outcome_var     = "y_binary",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  target_effect   = cal_target_or,
  outcome_type    = "binary",
  effect_measure  = "OR",
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  k_inter_range   = c(0, 3),
  grid_step       = 0.05,
  n_super         = 5000L,
  seed            = 8316951L,
  verbose         = TRUE
)

cat(sprintf("\n  OR(Q):   %.3f (target: %.1f)\n",
    dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup, cal_target_or))
cat(sprintf("  OR(Qc):  %.3f\n", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup))
cat(sprintf("  OR(ITT): %.3f\n", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$overall))
```

::: {.callout-note title="True harm subgroup Q — definition and calibrated effect"}
**Definition.** The data-generating harm subgroup is
$Q = \{\,\texttt{cd40} > 390 \;\text{and}\; \texttt{wtkg} > 80\,\}$,
encoded by the DGM markers `z1` ($\texttt{cd40} > 390$) and `z2`
($\texttt{wtkg} > 80$); a subject belongs to $Q$ only when **both** hold.

**Prevalence.** `r Q_n` of `r Q_N` subjects (`r sprintf("%.1f", Q_pct)`%) lie in $Q$.

**Calibrated treatment effect** (adverse odds-ratio scale):

- $\operatorname{OR}(Q) =$ `r sprintf("%.3f", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$harm_subgroup)` (target `r sprintf("%.1f", cal_target_or)`)
- $\operatorname{OR}(Q^{c}) =$ `r sprintf("%.3f", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$no_harm_subgroup)`
- $\operatorname{OR}(\text{ITT}) =$ `r sprintf("%.3f", dgm_calibrated$hazard_ratios$overall)`

Under the harm orientation, $Q$ is the region where the experimental arm
*raises* the adverse-event odds; $Q^{c}$ and the ITT population are calibrated
to be near-null by construction.
:::

```{r null-dgm}
dgm_null <- generate_glm_dgm(
  data            = actg_df,
  factor_vars     = dgm_factor_vars,
  continuous_vars = dgm_cont_vars,
  outcome_var     = "y_binary",
  treatment_var   = "treat",
  outcome_type    = "binary",
  subgroup_vars   = dgm_subgroup_vars,
  subgroup_cuts   = dgm_subgroup_cuts,
  model           = "null",
  n_super         = 5000L,
  seed            = 8316951L,
  verbose         = TRUE
)
```

#| eval: !expr run_single_trial

itt_fit <- glm(y_sim ~ treat_sim, family = "binomial", data = df_sim)
itt_OR <- exp(coef(itt_fit)["treat_sim"])
itt_event <- with(df_sim,mean(y_sim))

fs_params_single$parallel_args$workers <- n_workers

fs <- fs_single

if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm)) {

      round(timings$bootstrap_alt / 60, 1), "minutes\n")

  # Comprehensive summary with diagnostics.  All variables built here are
  # rendered by the small downstream chunks (single-trial-alt-render-*),
  # which exist solely so each gt table is the last (and only) expression
  # of its chunk -- the only way knitr's auto-print reliably emits raw
  # HTML for a gt_tbl object.
  summaries <- summarize_bootstrap_results(
    sgharm = fs$sg.harm,
    boot_results = fs_bc,
    create_plots = TRUE,

  ci_tab <- compute_frontier_cis(

  # Plot rendered inline here -- the graphics-device path is independent

  p <- plot_pareto_frontier(
    fs,

}

```{r single-trial-alt-manual-adjust-check}
#| eval: !expr run_single_trial
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Manual check: does the reported subgroup OR reflect cd40/wtkg adjustment? (click to expand)"
# Independent verification that the reported subgroup OR is on the COVARIATE-
# ADJUSTED scale.  We re-fit the within-subgroup treatment effect by hand --
# once unadjusted (y ~ treat) and once adjusted (y ~ treat + adjust_covariates)
# -- straight from glm(), and compare both to forestsearch's reported estimate.
# In an RCT the two manual fits still differ (the OR is non-collapsible), so the
# reported value matching the ADJUSTED fit is the signal that adjustment is live.
if (!is.null(fs$sg.harm) && !is.null(fs$df.est)) {
  .oc  <- fs$args_call_all$outcome.name
  .tr  <- fs$args_call_all$treat.name
  .adj <- fs$args_call_all$adjust_covariates
  if (is.null(.oc)) .oc <- "y_sim"
  if (is.null(.tr)) .tr <- "treat_sim"

  # Harm subgroup H = the "questionable" arm (treat.recommend == 0).
  dH <- fs$df.est[fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 0, , drop = FALSE]

  .or <- function(rhs) {
    f <- stats::as.formula(paste0(.oc, " ~ ", rhs))
    fit <- try(stats::glm(f, family = stats::binomial(), data = dH), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) return(NA_real_)
    exp(stats::coef(fit)[[.tr]])
  }

  or_unadj    <- .or(.tr)
  or_adj      <- if (length(.adj)) .or(paste(c(.tr, .adj), collapse = " + ")) else NA_real_
  # forestsearch's stored subgroup estimate (log-scale for GLM ratio measures).
  or_reported <- if (!is.null(fs$max_sg_est)) exp(fs$max_sg_est) else NA_real_

  cat(sprintf("Discovered subgroup : %s  (n = %d)\n",
              paste(fs$sg.harm, collapse = " & "), nrow(dH)))
  cat(sprintf("adjust_covariates   : %s\n",
              if (length(.adj)) paste(.adj, collapse = ", ") else "NULL"))
  cat(sprintf("  manual OR  unadjusted  [%s ~ %s]            : %.3f\n",
              .oc, .tr, or_unadj))
  cat(sprintf("  manual OR  adjusted    [%s ~ %s + %s] : %.3f\n",
              .oc, .tr, paste(.adj, collapse = " + "), or_adj))
  cat(sprintf("  forestsearch reported subgroup OR           : %.3f\n", or_reported))

  if (!is.na(or_adj) && !is.na(or_reported)) {
    d_adj   <- abs(or_reported - or_adj)
    d_unadj <- abs(or_reported - or_unadj)
    cat(sprintf("\n  |reported - adjusted|   = %.4f\n", d_adj))
    cat(sprintf("  |reported - unadjusted| = %.4f\n", d_unadj))
    cat(if (d_adj <= d_unadj)
          "  >>> reported tracks the ADJUSTED fit -> cd40/wtkg adjustment IS active.\n"
        else
          "  >>> reported tracks the UNADJUSTED fit -> adjustment NOT reflected; investigate.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No subgroup discovered in the alt trial; manual check skipped.\n")
}
```


## De-biased selection gate (Tier-2 test) {#sec-debias-gate}

The bootstrap above is the **Tier-1** (full nonparametric) bias-correction: it
re-runs the whole search on each resample. Here we compute the **Tier-2** fast
approximation of the same de-biased estimate — a multiplier bootstrap that reuses
the per-candidate `dfbeta` and re-applies the selection rule each draw, with no
refitting — and check it against the Tier-1 value for the subgroup this trial
selected. The de-biased estimate is then used as a *selection gate*: declare the
subgroup only if its de-biased effect clears a threshold. Because the correction
collapses spurious selections toward the null, such a gate mitigates the
search-level false-discovery rate; because it over-shrinks true effects, the gate
is set near the null (OR > 1), not at the screening threshold.

```{r debias-gate-setup}
#| include: false
.dg_files <- c("fdr_family_multiplier.R", "fdr_calibration.R", "fdr_debias_gate.R")
.dg_dir   <- getOption("fdr_src_dir", ".")
.dg_ok    <- all(file.exists(file.path(.dg_dir, .dg_files)))
if (.dg_ok) invisible(lapply(file.path(.dg_dir, .dg_files), source))
run_debias_gate_eval <- isTRUE(run_debias_gate) && isTRUE(.dg_ok) && !is.null(fs$sg.harm)

# Factor family reproducing the search candidate space (continuous covariates
# cut at q1/median/q3 both sides, binaries both levels); unique() collapses tied
# quantiles, matching the search's redundant-cut handling.
.dg_factors <- function(df, cont = cont_vars, bin = bin_vars) {
  f <- list()
  for (v in cont) {
    qs   <- unique(stats::quantile(df[[v]], c(.25, .5, .75), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE))
    labs <- c("q1", "med", "q3")[seq_along(qs)]
    for (k in seq_along(qs)) {
      f[[sprintf("%s<=%s", v, labs[k])]] <- df[[v]] <= qs[k]
      f[[sprintf("%s>%s",  v, labs[k])]] <- df[[v]] >  qs[k]
    }
  }
  for (v in bin) { f[[sprintf("%s=1", v)]] <- df[[v]] == 1; f[[sprintf("%s=0", v)]] <- df[[v]] == 0 }
  f
}
```

```{r debias-gate-test}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# Wrapped in local() so chunk-internal names (cands, spec, infl, ...) never leak
# into the global environment and collide with later chunks (e.g. the Pareto
# appendix's data.table `cands`).
local({
if (!run_debias_gate_eval) {
  cat(if (is.null(fs$sg.harm))
        "_De-biased gate test skipped: no subgroup discovered in this trial._\n"
      else if (!isTRUE(run_debias_gate))
        "_De-biased gate test skipped (`run_debias_gate = FALSE`)._\n"
      else
        paste0("_De-biased gate test skipped: place `fdr_family_multiplier.R`, ",
               "`fdr_calibration.R`, and `fdr_debias_gate.R` beside this document ",
               "(or set `options(fdr_src_dir = \"<dir>\")`)._\n"))
} else {
  spec <- list(outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR", treat.name = "treat_sim",
               outcome.name = "y_sim", offset.name = NULL,
               adjust_covariates = fs_adjust_covariates, adverse_outcome = TRUE)
  dg_maxk <- if (!is.null(fs_params$maxk)) fs_params$maxk else 2L
  # The de-bias re-selection uses the consistency-maximizing rule -- the
  # canonical, stable choice validated against the literal bootstrap.  The
  # observed selected subgroup itself (passed as selected_index below) is the
  # document's effMaxSG pick and is what gets de-biased; matching the exact
  # effMaxSG neighborhood in the bootstrap re-selection is a future refinement
  # (the naive max-effect band over-corrects on the full reconstructed family).
  dg_rule <- "maxcons"

  # Candidate family + the observed selected subgroup (from its cut definition).
  facs   <- .dg_factors(df_sim)
  cands  <- enumerate_candidates(df_sim, facs, maxk = dg_maxk, min_n = 60L,
                                 min_events_per_arm = 10L,
                                 treat.name = "treat_sim", outcome.name = "y_sim")
  H_lab  <- paste(fs$sg.harm, collapse = " & ")
  Hmem   <- tryCatch(which(with(df_sim, eval(parse(text = H_lab)))),
                     error = function(e) integer(0))
  if (length(Hmem) >= 30L) cands[[H_lab]] <- Hmem

  .t0      <- proc.time()
  infl     <- build_influence_matrix(df_sim, cands, spec)
  t_build  <- as.numeric((proc.time() - .t0)["elapsed"])
  sel_idx  <- match(H_lab, infl$names)
  sizes   <- vapply(seq_len(infl$n_usable), function(g) sum(infl$B[, g] != 0), numeric(1))

  if (is.na(sel_idx)) {
    cat(sprintf("_Selected subgroup `%s` could not be re-fit in the reconstructed family; test skipped._\n", H_lab))
  } else {
    .t0 <- proc.time()
    dg <- debias_family_multiplier(
      infl$B, infl$beta_hat, infl$sigma_D, sizes,
      c_screen = log(fs_effect_threshold), c_consistency = log(fs_consistency_threshold),
      p_star = fs_pconsistency_threshold, selection = dg_rule,
      effect_neighborhood = effect_neighborhood, selected_index = sel_idx,
      draws = 4000L, multiplier = "poisson", seed = 1L)
    t_debias <- as.numeric((proc.time() - .t0)["elapsed"])

    # Tier-1 full-bootstrap estimates (point + CI) for the harm subgroup H,
    # read from fs_bc$H_estimates (H0 = naive, H2 = bias-corrected; *_lower/_upper
    # are the bootstrap / infinitesimal-jackknife limits).
    .fld <- function(o, n) tryCatch(as.numeric(o[[n]]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    H0 <- .fld(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H0"); H0l <- .fld(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H0_lower"); H0u <- .fld(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H0_upper")
    H2 <- .fld(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H2"); H2l <- .fld(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H2_lower"); H2u <- .fld(fs_bc$H_estimates, "H2_upper")
    # Tier-2 CIs: exp(beta +/- 1.96 * robust SE).  Approximate -- the SE is the
    # subgroup's robust treatment SE and does NOT carry the selection-adjusted
    # variance that Tier 1's infinitesimal-jackknife CI captures.
    n2l <- exp(dg$beta_naive    - stats::qnorm(0.975) * dg$se)
    n2u <- exp(dg$beta_naive    + stats::qnorm(0.975) * dg$se)
    t2l <- exp(dg$beta_debiased - stats::qnorm(0.975) * dg$se)
    t2u <- exp(dg$beta_debiased + stats::qnorm(0.975) * dg$se)
    .ci <- function(e, l, u) if (all(is.finite(c(e, l, u)))) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", e, l, u) else sprintf("%.2f", e)

    cat(sprintf("\nSelected subgroup: **%s** (n = %d). Rule: `%s`. ",
                H_lab, length(Hmem), dg_rule))
    cat(sprintf("Bootstrap selection rate %.2f; fast selection bias %.4f (log scale).\n\n",
                dg$selection_rate, dg$selection_bias))

    comp <- data.frame(
      quantity = c("naive OR (95% CI)", "de-biased OR (95% CI)"),
      `Tier 2 (fast multiplier)` = c(.ci(dg$effect_naive, n2l, n2u), .ci(dg$effect_debiased, t2l, t2u)),
      `Tier 1 (full bootstrap)`  = c(.ci(H0, H0l, H0u),              .ci(H2, H2l, H2u)),
      check.names = FALSE)
    cat(knitr::kable(comp, row.names = FALSE), sep = "\n"); cat("\n\n")
    cat("The naive-OR row is a scale sanity check (both fit the same adjusted ",
        "logistic on the selected subgroup); agreement on the de-biased row is ",
        "the Tier-2-vs-Tier-1 validation. The Tier-2 CI is approximate: it uses ",
        "the subgroup's robust SE and so is narrower than the Tier-1 ",
        "infinitesimal-jackknife CI, which carries the selection-adjusted variance.\n\n",
        sep = "")

    # Timing.  Tier 1 is the full bootstrap above (timings$bootstrap_alt); Tier 2
    # is the family build plus the multiplier de-bias.  The build re-fits every
    # candidate and is reconstruction overhead that would be ~0 if integrated
    # into the search (which already fits each candidate); the marginal Tier-2
    # cost is the de-bias step.
    t_tier1 <- if (!is.null(timings$bootstrap_alt)) as.numeric(timings$bootstrap_alt) else NA_real_
    cat("Computational timing:\n\n")
    if (is.finite(t_tier1))
      cat(sprintf("- Tier 1 (full bootstrap): %.1f s (%.1f min)\n", t_tier1, t_tier1 / 60))
    cat(sprintf("- Tier 2 de-bias (4000 draws): %.2f s | family rebuild: %.2f s\n",
                t_debias, t_build))
    if (is.finite(t_tier1) && t_debias > 0)
      cat(sprintf("- Speedup: **%.0fx** (de-bias only); **%.0fx** (incl. family rebuild)\n\n",
                  t_tier1 / t_debias, t_tier1 / (t_build + t_debias)))

    cat("Gate decisions:\n\n")
    for (tg in c(1.00, 1.10, 1.25)) {
      d <- gated_declare(dg, t_gate = tg, gate = "point")
      cat(sprintf("- OR > %.2f (point): de-biased OR %.2f -> **%s**\n",
                  tg, dg$effect_debiased, if (d) "DECLARE" else "reject"))
    }
    dci <- gated_declare(dg, t_gate = 1.0, gate = "ci")
    cat(sprintf("- CI lower bound > 1.0: lower %.2f -> **%s**\n",
                dg$ci_lower_debiased, if (dci) "DECLARE" else "reject"))
  }
}
})
```

A gate near the null (OR > 1) keeps a genuine harm subgroup — whose de-biased
estimate stays elevated — while rejecting spurious ones, whose de-biased estimate
collapses toward the ITT effect. The Tier-2 figures here are a fast, leading-order
approximation of the Tier-1 bootstrap: the family is reconstructed from the
quartile-cut candidate space, the bias term uses the consistency-maximizing
re-selection (validated against a literal bootstrap in `fdr_debias_gate.R`'s
demo), and the comparison conditions on this trial's selected subgroup. Treat a
close de-biased-OR row as confirmation that Tier 2 tracks Tier 1; a large gap
flags that the selection-rule approximation needs refinement before the gate is
trusted for this configuration.

## Consistency method check: split vs. resample {#sec-method-check}

The single trial above ran under `consistency_method = "resample"`.  Here the
identical flagship configuration is re-run under **both** settings on the same
simulated trial --- data, screening engines, thresholds, adjustment, and seed
all fixed --- so only the consistency step differs.  For this binary/OR
outcome `"resample"` engages the logistic influence-function approximation
(single fit per candidate; rate
$2\Phi((\hat\beta - \log c_2)/\sigma_D) - 1$).  The two methods should select
the same subgroup, with per-candidate consistency rates agreeing to within the
documented approximation error (mean $|\text{error}| \approx 0.02$ for OR).

```{r method-check-run}
#| eval: !expr run_single_trial && fs_run_method_compare
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Re-run flagship arm under split vs. resample (click to expand)"
# Re-run the flagship single-trial configuration under each consistency method.
# fs_params_single already carries every other setting; only the consistency
# method is overridden, mirroring the GBSG split-vs-resample comparison.
run_fs_method <- function(method) {
  p <- fs_params_single
  p$consistency_method <- method
  t0 <- proc.time()
  fit <- do.call(forestsearch, c(
    list(df.analysis = df_sim, confounders.name = confounders), p))
  future::plan("sequential")
  list(fs = fit, elapsed = unname((proc.time() - t0)["elapsed"]))
}

res_split    <- run_fs_method("split")
res_resample <- run_fs_method("resample")

summ_method <- function(tag, r) {
  fs   <- r$fs
  sg   <- if (is.null(fs$sg.harm)) "(none)" else paste(fs$sg.harm, collapse = " & ")
  size <- if (!is.null(fs$df.est)) sum(fs$df.est$treat.recommend == 0) else NA_integer_
  data.frame(method = tag, subgroup = sg, size = size,
             elapsed_sec = round(r$elapsed, 2))
}

method_cmp <- rbind(summ_method("split", res_split),
                    summ_method("resample", res_resample))
print(method_cmp, row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nIdentical selected subgroup? ",
    identical(res_split$fs$sg.harm, res_resample$fs$sg.harm), "\n")
```

  sg_tables(res_split$fs, ndecimals = 3, which_df = "est")$sg10_out
```

```

#| eval: !expr run_single_trial

# Timing Summary

```{r timing}
#| echo: false

# Comprehensive timing summary: aggregates bootstrap, LOO, and
# simulation-loop wall-clock times across H1 and H0 branches.  Any slot
# left unset (e.g. when fs$sg.harm is NULL and the bootstrap was
# skipped, or when run_loo = FALSE) is rendered as "—" in the table.
#
# In sim_mode == "import", t_alt/t_null are restored from the bundle's
# meta block (see mode-handoff chunk); bootstrap and LOO timings come
# from the current session's computation chunks.

# Defensive: timings list should exist from the setup chunk; create
# empty if for some reason it doesn't (e.g. caller skipping setup).
if (!exists("timings", inherits = FALSE) || !is.list(timings)) {
  timings <- list()
}

# Convert a stored seconds value to minutes; return NA when not set.
.timing_min <- function(slot) {
  v <- timings[[slot]]
  if (is.null(v) || !is.numeric(v) || length(v) == 0L || is.na(v)) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  as.numeric(v) / 60
}

sim_alt_min  <- if (exists("t_alt",  inherits = FALSE) &&
                    is.numeric(t_alt))  t_alt  / 60 else NA_real_
sim_null_min <- if (exists("t_null", inherits = FALSE) &&
                    is.numeric(t_null)) t_null / 60 else NA_real_

# Per-branch component breakdown
bs_alt  <- .timing_min("bootstrap_alt")
loo_alt <- .timing_min("loo_alt")
bs_nul  <- .timing_min("bootstrap_null")
loo_nul <- .timing_min("loo_null")

subtotal_alt  <- sum(c(bs_alt,  loo_alt,  sim_alt_min),  na.rm = TRUE)
subtotal_null <- sum(c(bs_nul,  loo_nul,  sim_null_min), na.rm = TRUE)
grand_total   <- subtotal_alt + subtotal_null

timing_dt <- data.frame(
  Component  = c("Bootstrap (single-trial)",
                 "LOO cross-validation",
                 "Simulation loop",
                 "Subtotal"),
  H1         = c(bs_alt,  loo_alt,  sim_alt_min,  subtotal_alt),
  H0         = c(bs_nul,  loo_nul,  sim_null_min, subtotal_null),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

timing_gt <- gt::gt(timing_dt) |>
  gt::tab_header(
    title    = "Timing Summary (wall-clock minutes)",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Mode = %s; nsims_alt = %d, nsims_null = %d; total runtime = %.2f min (%.2f hr)",
      sim_mode, nsims_alt, nsims_null,
      grand_total, grand_total / 60)
  ) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    Component = "Component",
    H1        = "H1 (alt)",
    H0        = "H0 (null)"
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c("H1", "H0"), decimals = 2) |>
  gt::sub_missing(columns = c("H1", "H0"), missing_text = "—") |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style     = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_body(rows = Component == "Subtotal")
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style     = gt::cell_borders(sides = "top", weight = gt::px(2)),
    locations = gt::cells_body(rows = Component == "Subtotal")
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    sprintf("Subtotals sum the three components per branch; '—' indicates a section that did not run (e.g. no harm subgroup identified, or run_loo = FALSE).")
  )

# Reset parallel plan before emitting the table (side-effect call
# placed first so the gt object is the final expression -- this is the
# only path knitr auto-prints reliably for gt_tbl).
plan(sequential)

timing_gt
```

# Appendix: The Pareto frontier in subgroup selection

# The dominance rule

Both objectives --- effect size and sample size --- are *maximized*. A
candidate $i$ is **dominated** if some other candidate $j$ is at least as
good on both axes and strictly better on at least one:

$$
\text{dominated}(i) \;\Longleftrightarrow\;
\exists\, j \neq i:\;
\mathrm{hr}_j \ge \mathrm{hr}_i \;\wedge\; N_j \ge N_i
\;\wedge\; (\mathrm{hr}_j > \mathrm{hr}_i \;\vee\; N_j > N_i).
$$

The **Pareto frontier** is the set of non-dominated candidates --- the
upper-right boundary of the cloud. The package implements this as an
$O(n^2)$ scan in `.pareto_dominated_xy()`; candidates with a missing
effect or size are treated as dominated. The function below is a
faithful mirror of that internal helper, kept local so this document
renders without the package; the validation section confirms the two
agree.

```{r dominance}
# Mirror of forestsearch internal .pareto_dominated_xy(): both axes maximized.
dominated_xy <- function(x, y) {
  n <- length(x)
  dom <- logical(n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (is.na(x[i]) || is.na(y[i])) { dom[i] <- TRUE; next }
    for (j in seq_len(n)) {
      if (i == j) next
      if (is.na(x[j]) || is.na(y[j])) next
      if (x[j] >= x[i] && y[j] >= y[i] && (x[j] > x[i] || y[j] > y[i])) {
        dom[i] <- TRUE
        break
      }
    }
  }
  dom
}
```

# How the band is formed

`.compute_inclusion_band()` builds two indicators and multiplies them:

```r
in_nbhd   <- (hr >= (1 - effect_neighborhood) * max(hr))   # 1-D effect band
in_pareto <- !dominated_xy(hr, N)                          # 2-D frontier
in_band   <- in_nbhd * in_pareto
```

Each `selection_rule` switches the two components on or off:

| `selection_rule` | `in_nbhd` | `in_pareto` | `in_band` is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"neighborhood"` | active | all ones | the effect band only |
| `"pareto"` | all ones | active | the frontier only |
| `"both"` | active | active | their intersection |

For ratio measures stored on the log scale (GLM OR/IRR), `hr` is
exponentiated before either test so the comparison is on the natural
scale; Cox HR is already natural. The neighborhood floor is a *relative*
tolerance: with `effect_neighborhood = 0.10` a candidate is in-band iff
its effect is within 10% of the strongest effect among the survivors.
Setting it to `0` collapses the band to a strict max-effect filter.

# From inclusion to selection

`sort_subgroups()` orders the candidates by a five-key lexicographic
sort and takes the top row. For `"hrMaxSG"` the key is

$$
(-\,\texttt{in\_band},\; -N,\; -\texttt{Pcons},\; -\texttt{hr},\; K),
$$

so: in-band candidates first; then the largest $N$; then higher
consistency; then higher effect; then fewer factors. `"hrMinSG"` is
identical except $N$ is minimized. Only `in_band` depends on
`selection_rule` --- the sort itself is fixed.

For the worked set, every rule that keeps `C` selects it (largest $N$ in
the band), so the **top pick is `C`** under `"neighborhood"` and
`"both"` alike; the rules differ only in whether `E` carries an in-band
flag in the diagnostic table.

## Where the rules genuinely diverge

The top selection differs only in a narrow corner: when two candidates
**tie on the maximum band $N$**, because the sort breaks $N$-ties by
consistency *before* effect, whereas Pareto dominance looks only at
(effect, $N$).

```{r corner}
corner <- data.table(
  id    = c("T", "D"),
  Pcons = c(0.95, 0.80),
  hr    = c(2.30, 2.45),
  N     = c(150L, 150L),
  K     = c(1L,   1L)
)
corner[]
```

`D` dominates `T` (equal $N$, higher HR). Under `"neighborhood"` both are
in-band, they tie on $N$, and the consistency tier keeps the
higher-`Pcons` candidate `T`. Under `"both"`, `T` is off the frontier and
excluded, so the higher-effect `D` is selected.

```{r corner-eval}
if (have_fs) {
  top_pick <- function(rule) {
    s <- forestsearch::sort_subgroups(
      data.table::copy(corner), "hrMaxSG",
      selection_rule = rule, effect_neighborhood = EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
    s$id[1L]
  }
  data.table(selection_rule = c("neighborhood", "both"),
             top_pick = vapply(c("neighborhood", "both"), top_pick, character(1)))
} else {
  cat("forestsearch not installed; expected: neighborhood -> T, both -> D.\n")
}
```

So `"both"` refuses to settle on a point another candidate beats on both
axes, even when it won the consistency tie; `"neighborhood"` will keep
the higher-consistency point.

# Validation against the package

Confirm the local frontier and band computations agree with the
shipped internals, and that `compute_pareto_frontier()` returns the
expected non-dominated rows.

```{r validate}
if (have_fs) {
  .ok <- function(lbl, cond)
    cat(if (isTRUE(cond)) "PASS" else "FAIL", "-", lbl, "\n")

  dt_hn <- cands[, .(hr, N)]

  pkg_dom <- forestsearch:::pareto_dominated_flags(dt_hn)
  .ok("dominated flags match .pareto_dominated_xy mirror",
      identical(pkg_dom, cands$dominated))

  pkg_nbhd <- forestsearch:::.compute_inclusion_band(
    cands$hr, cands$N, "neighborhood", EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
  .ok("neighborhood band matches",
      identical(as.logical(pkg_nbhd), cands$in_nbhd))

  pkg_both <- forestsearch:::.compute_inclusion_band(
    cands$hr, cands$N, "both", EFFECT_NEIGHBORHOOD)
  .ok("both band matches in_nbhd & on_frontier",
      identical(as.logical(pkg_both), cands$in_both))

  fr <- forestsearch:::compute_pareto_frontier(dt_hn)
  .ok("compute_pareto_frontier returns the non-dominated set",
      setequal(fr$hr, cands[on_frontier == TRUE, hr]))
} else {
  cat("forestsearch not installed; validation skipped.\n")
}
```

# Practical guidance

* `"neighborhood"` (default) asks only "is the effect close to the
  best?" then maximizes $N$. It can keep a high-consistency candidate
  that another point beats on both effect and size.
* `"pareto"` removes the `effect_neighborhood` tuning parameter
  entirely and selects on the (effect, $N$) trade-off alone --- but
  without the effect floor it will admit large-$N$, weak-effect points
  (like `F`) that the band is designed to exclude.
* `"both"` is the conservative choice: it keeps the effect floor *and*
  refuses dominated points. The in-band set under `"both"` is always a
  subset of the one under `"neighborhood"`.

The frontier here is an inclusion filter, not a stand-alone selection
criterion: the chosen subgroup still comes from the five-key sort, and
under `"hrMinSG"` the selected point may deliberately be $N$-dominated
(small subgroups are preferred). For a post-hoc *reporting* view of the
frontier independent of `sg_focus`, use `compute_pareto_frontier()` /
`pareto_frontier_table()`.

## Relationship to `dina_subgroup()`

The DINA `effMaxSG`/`effMinSG` foci reuse the same
`.compute_inclusion_band()` core, but only with
`selection_rule = "neighborhood"` --- DINA's univariate threshold
candidates form a simple effect-versus-size trade-off where the 1-D band
suffices. The `"pareto"`/`"both"` frontier variants are forestsearch-only
today; extending them to DINA would be a deliberate addition.
